note: Supplement to the Hyundai/Kia family table, covering the engines whose codes follow neither the G-prefix petrol nor D-prefix diesel convention and so kept the fabricated 'Asian OEM Standard' approval. Most are Mazda-derived units from Kia's Ford/Mazda period — the B-series petrols in the Pride and Sephia, the FE in the Clarus and Sportage, and the RF and R2 diesels — plus Kia's own J2, the 2.7 diesel in the K2700 and Pregio that is everywhere in Tunisia as a light truck and was recorded as petrol. Hyundai's DJY is PSA's XUD9 diesel, fitted to the Lantra, and is given the same figures as the PSA table uses for it.

engines.source: Kia J2 2.7 indirect-injection diesel — K2700, Pregio, Besta. Recorded as petrol. Pre-common-rail with no particulate filter, so a conventional 15W-40 is correct and suits hot climates; the capacity is a family figure rather than a manual one.
Mazda-derived RF 2.0 and R2 2.2 diesels — Sportage, Retona, Carnival, Besta. Capacity is a family figure.
DJY is PSA's XUD9A 1.9 diesel, fitted to the Hyundai Lantra, and was recorded as petrol here exactly as it was under Peugeot. Same 4.75 L change capacity and 10W-40 grade as the PSA entry.
1.0 three-cylinder — Picanto, i10. Small sump; capacity is a family estimate.
Mazda B-series 1.3-1.6 petrol — Pride, Sephia, Shuma, Avella, Carens. Pre-1998 designs; 10W-40 is the conventional grade and suits hot climates. Capacity is a family estimate.
Mazda-derived FE 2.0 and the 1.8 units — Clarus, Sportage, Retona, Sephia, Elantra. Capacity is a family estimate.
Kia's own 1.3/1.5 petrols — Rio, Avella. Capacity is a family estimate.
2.4/2.5 petrol — Carnival, Sonata. Capacity is a family estimate.
Hyundai's 4.5-5.0 V8 — Equus / Centennial. Capacity is a family estimate.
